paragraphs.title: Abner's Death and the Weakening of Ish-bosheth's Kingdom

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “his hands were feeble.”
easy.q: What happened to Ish-bosheth when he heard that Abner was dead?

easy.explanation: The verse says that “all the Israelites were troubled.”
easy.q: How did all the Israelites respond to Abner's death?

answers: Captains of bands under Saul's son
easy.explanation: They are introduced as “captains of bands” serving Saul's son.

answers: Abner had been a major power in the kingdom
Abner was a stranger to the kingdom
Abner had no connection with the government
medium.explanation: The reaction shows that Abner had been an important support of Ish-bosheth's rule.
medium.q: What can be understood from Ish-bosheth's weakness and Israel's trouble after Abner's death?

answers: People living in a place as temporary or resident strangers
medium.explanation: Sojourners are people residing in a place without being its original inhabitants.
medium.q: In the phrase “were sojourners there,” what does “sojourners” mean?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin.”
medium.q: What does the passage say about Beeroth's relationship to Benjamin?

challenge.explanation: Ish-bosheth's feeble hands and Israel's trouble show that his kingdom was shaken.
challenge.q: What result of Abner's death is emphasized at the beginning of the chapter?

answers: To emphasize their connection with Beeroth and Benjamin
To describe their war with the Philistines
challenge.explanation: These details identify their background and explain the status of the people from Beeroth.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention Rechab and Baanah's origin and the flight of the Beerothites?

answers: Abner's death, the Beerothites' flight, Israel's trouble
Israel's trouble, Abner's death, the Beerothites' flight
Abner's death, Ish-bosheth's weakness and Israel's trouble
challenge.explanation: The passage first mentions Abner's death and then describes Ish-bosheth's and Israel's reactions.
challenge.q: Which sequence is correct according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The verse identifies Mephibosheth as Jonathan's son.

answers: He was lame in his feet
He was injured as an adult
easy.explanation: The KJV says that he “was lame of his feet.”
easy.q: What was wrong with Mephibosheth's feet?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “his nurse took him up, and fled.”
easy.q: Who carried Mephibosheth when his nurse fled?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “He was five years old.”
medium.q: How old was Mephibosheth when news came of Saul and Jonathan?

answers: He fell when his nurse made haste to flee
He became ill as a child
medium.explanation: His nurse carried him while fleeing, and he fell as she hurried.
medium.q: What caused Mephibosheth to become lame?

answers: A woman who cared for and carried him
medium.explanation: His nurse was the woman responsible for caring for him and carrying him during the flight.
medium.q: What does “nurse” mean in this passage?

answers: It introduces another member of Saul's house
It explains Rechab and Baanah's origin
challenge.explanation: The narrative pauses to introduce Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son.
challenge.q: What is the role of the verse about Mephibosheth in the chapter's narrative?

answers: The news caused his nurse to flee in haste
The news caused Mephibosheth to go to war
The news brought him to Hebron
challenge.explanation: After hearing the news, his nurse fled with him, and he fell during the flight.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the news of Saul and Jonathan's deaths and Mephibosheth's injury?

challenge.explanation: The verse concludes, “And his name was Mephibosheth.”
challenge.q: Which detail about Mephibosheth might easily be overlooked but appears in the verse?

paragraphs.title: The Murder of Ish-bosheth and the Assassins' Escape

easy.explanation: Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, came to his house.
easy.q: Who came to the house of Ish-bosheth?

answers: About the heat of the day
easy.explanation: The KJV says they came “about the heat of the day.”
easy.q: When did Rechab and Baanah come to Ish-bosheth's house?

easy.explanation: They took his head and escaped through the plain toward Hebron.
easy.q: Where did Rechab and Baanah go after killing Ish-bosheth?

answers: As though they had come to fetch wheat
medium.explanation: They came into the house “as though they would have fetched wheat.”
medium.q: How did Rechab and Baanah enter the house, according to the apparent meaning of the passage?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes Ish-bosheth resting during the middle of the day.
medium.q: What does “his bed at noon” describe?

answers: They took his head and escaped all night
medium.explanation: They beheaded him, took his head, and got away through the plain all night.
medium.q: What did Rechab and Baanah do after killing Ish-bosheth?

answers: They came during his midday rest and entered as if fetching wheat
They arrived at the head of an army
challenge.explanation: His midday rest and their apparent pretense of fetching wheat gave them access to him.
challenge.q: Which combination of details explains how they reached Ish-bosheth?

answers: They intended to remain in the house
They were trying to reach Hebron quickly
They planned to return to Beeroth
challenge.explanation: Traveling all night indicates that they were hurrying toward Hebron.
challenge.q: What does their escape through the plain all night suggest about their purpose?

answers: The wording about coming into the house and the house guard
challenge.explanation: The wording of verse 6 has been understood in more than one way, including a possible reference to the house guard.
challenge.q: Which detail allows an alternative interpretation concerning their entrance into the house?

paragraphs.title: The Head Brought to David and the Claim of Vengeance

easy.explanation: They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David in Hebron.
easy.q: To whom did Rechab and Baanah bring Ish-bosheth's head?

answers: As David's enemy who sought his life
easy.explanation: They called him “the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life.”
easy.q: How did Rechab and Baanah describe Ish-bosheth to David?

easy.explanation: David said he took hold of and slew the youth “in Ziklag.”
easy.q: Where did David say he killed the Amalekite youth?

answers: That it was vengeance against David's enemy
That it was commanded by Abner
medium.explanation: They claimed that the LORD had avenged David against Saul and his seed.
medium.q: What did Rechab and Baanah claim about the killing of Ish-bosheth?

answers: To show that he killed a messenger who expected a reward for reporting Saul's death
To explain the youth's family origin
medium.explanation: David recalled that the youth reported Saul's death and expected a reward, but David killed him.
medium.q: Why did David mention the Amalekite youth?

answers: David was swearing by the LORD
medium.explanation: David began his answer with an oath invoking the LORD.
medium.q: What is the significance of David's words, “As the LORD liveth”?

answers: He rewarded everyone who killed a rival
Killing a rival is not necessarily an act deserving reward
He did not remember Saul's death
challenge.explanation: David used the story to reject the assassins' claim that their deed deserved a reward.
challenge.q: What did David intend to make clear by telling the story of the Amalekite youth?

answers: They presented the killing as useful vengeance, but David viewed it as wrong
They wanted to flee, but David helped them
They denied the killing, but David believed them
challenge.explanation: The assassins called the act vengeance, while David condemned it as wicked.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the assassins' words and David's response?

answers: That he was Saul's son and David's enemy
challenge.explanation: They emphasized that Ish-bosheth was Saul's son and had sought David's life.
challenge.q: Which detail about Ish-bosheth did the assassins try to use to justify their deed?

paragraphs.title: David Punishes the Assassins and Buries Ish-bosheth

easy.q: What did David call Rechab and Baanah?

answers: They were to be appointed as captains
easy.explanation: David commanded his young men to slay them.
easy.q: What did David command to be done to Rechab and Baanah?

easy.explanation: The head was buried “in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.”

answers: Because they killed a righteous person in his own house upon his bed
Because they arrived late in Hebron
medium.explanation: David condemned them for killing a righteous person in his own house and on his bed.
medium.q: Why did David consider Rechab and Baanah worthy of punishment?

answers: They were buried in Abner's sepulchre
Their hands and feet were cut off, and they were hanged up
They were sent back to Beeroth
medium.explanation: David's young men cut off their hands and feet and hanged them over the pool.
medium.q: What was done to the assassins after they were killed?

answers: Remove them from the land by death
medium.explanation: David means that the wicked men would be removed from the earth.
medium.q: What does David mean by “take you away from the earth”?

answers: He punished the assassins but arranged for Ish-bosheth's head to be buried
He punished Ish-bosheth and buried the assassins
challenge.explanation: David executed the murderers while ensuring that Ish-bosheth's head received burial.
challenge.q: What was the difference between David's treatment of the assassins and his treatment of Ish-bosheth's head?

answers: Public disgrace and display of punishment
challenge.explanation: Their bodies were publicly displayed as a sign of disgrace and judgment.
challenge.q: What did hanging the assassins' bodies over the pool express?

answers: Murdering a person in his own house is serious even if he is an enemy
challenge.explanation: David emphasized the seriousness of killing a righteous and innocent person in his own home.
challenge.q: What moral principle emerges from David's words?
